subject: Re: OwlLM weights - hosting & redistribution licensing
messages:
From: Kai Nakamura <kai@openweights.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia@modelhub.co>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: OwlLM weights - question about hosting & redistribution

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the intro last week. OpenWeights Labs is evaluating a handful of partners to distribute our OwlLM family (7B/13B) more broadly — specifically to let enterprise customers deploy models quickly via partners that can both host inference and, in limited cases, provide the model weights under controlled redistribution.

Two quick things we wanted to clarify about Redwood's capabilities and guardrails before we schedule a technical walkthrough:

- Does Redwood support a model distribution arrangement where you host the canonical weights in your infra and also offer a mechanism that allows certain vetted customers to run the weights in their VPC/on-prem under a partner redistribution license?
- If yes, what controls do you impose around the weights (e.g., no re-upload outside managed infra, watermarking/provenance, KMS protection, attestations)?

We can share a short draft of the redistribution license we typically start from (it's custom; not plain OSS). I've attached a product overview and the API spec. Would love to jump on a 30-min call next week with your partnerships or legal lead.

Best,
Kai
Head of Ecosystem, OpenWeights Labs

Attachments: OpenWeights_Tech_Overview.pdf, OpenWeights_API_Spec.xlsx
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Nakamura <kai@openweights.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OwlLM weights - question about hosting & redistribution

Kai —

Appreciate the note and the materials. Short answer: yes, Redwood supports both hosted inference and partner-managed redistribution patterns, but the specifics matter a lot and we typically formalize them in a Partner Addendum that sits on top of our standard platform T&Cs.

A few clarifying Qs so we come prepared to a call:
- Is OpenWeights planning to permit unrestricted redistribution to third parties, or a limited redistribution to customers vetted by OpenWeights and Redwood?
- Do you require us to hand over raw weights to customers, or is the requirement to enable customer instances that reference a Redwood-hosted canonical weights image?
- Any export control or country blacklist constraints we should be aware of?

Operational controls we commonly use: KMS-backed key management (we can integrate with customer KMS in Private deployments), signed manifests + provenance metadata, per-customer SLO/usage limits, and optional model watermarking for tracing. From a licensing perspective we usually support: inference-only, hosted-hosting-with-restricted-redistribution (limited to vetted customers), or a bespoke redistribution license with indemnity and audit rights.

I've looped in Jonas (partner ops) and Aditya (legal) so we can sketch negotiation points and a draft term set. Proposed next steps: 1) 30-min sync with your engineering and legal folks; 2) we exchange a short Partner Addendum draft; 3) 2-week tech due diligence (security + load test). Does Nov 18 or 19 work for a call?

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

--

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 15:21:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: OwlLM redistribution - proposed commercial/ops guardrails

Vanessa / Aditya —

Quick notes after skimming the overview: I think this is an interesting partner but the distribution ask raises a few red flags we should scope up before the call. My suggested position:

- Default acceptable model distribution modes: 1) Hosted inference (no weights redistribution) — straightforward; 2) Vetted redistribution to named enterprise customers only, via Redwood-managed image / signed artifact; 3) No open redistribution (we should not allow seeds for public rehosting).
- Controls we should require from OpenWeights: signed manifest + provenance header in artifact, per-weight checksums, tamper-proof signing (they can sign with an org key we register), and a minimum of SOC2 evidence for their build pipeline.
- Commercial: per-instance redistribution fee (annual), storage fee for weights snapshots (per-GB/month), and an SLO credit pool to cover support for redistributed instances. Also carve-outs for export control compliance — if they have blacklisted countries we block routing.

Open legal items for Aditya: indemnity for IP misuses, audit and review rights for redistributed deployments, and a clause preventing downstream re-redistribution by customers. Also we should limit the scenario where raw weights are distributed to customer-managed on-prem (that greatly increases risk). If we must allow it, require escrow/escrowed-release only after KYC + inspection and strong indemnities.

Thoughts? I can draft a short commercial term sheet to hand the partner on the call.

— Jonas
Director, Partner Ops

On Thu, Nov 13, 2025 at 15:40, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jon, Vanessa —

> Thanks for the summary. From a legal perspective: we should aim to avoid open redistribution. The most defensible path is either: (A) inference-only license; or (B) redistribution under a contract that requires the partner (OpenWeights) to transfer a signed, immutable artifact to Redwood; Redwood then grants named-customer redistribution rights (no further redistribution).
>
> Key redline items: export controls clause, explicit prohibition on customer-driven re-uploads to public repos, audit rights, and clear indemnity. We'll also require model provenance + SBOM for the weights build if they want redistribution privileges.
>
> I can overlay these into the partner addendum draft — aim to keep the commercial terms neutral and put legal protections in the addendum.
>
> — Aditya
> Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Kai Nakamura <kai@openweights.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed partner approach: OwlLM redistribution & hosting (next steps)

Kai —

Thanks for the materials and for waiting while we scoped internally. Below is a concise proposal from Redwood on how we can work together to enable wider distribution of OwlLM while protecting both parties and downstream customers.

High-level commercial & ops proposal (summary):
- Permitted modes: 1) Hosted inference via Redwood Hosted API (standard); 2) Redistribution to named, vetted enterprise customers ("named-customer redistribution") where Redwood supplies a signed, canonical weights image that the customer runs within a Redwood-managed deployment or a Redwood-sanctioned Private deployment.
- Restricted redistribution constraints: no public re-uploads; no transfer of raw weights to uncontrolled public repos; customers may run weights in their VPC only if the deployment is registered and bound to the signed manifest + attestation.
- Security controls: KMS-backed key wrapping (we can integrate with customer KMS), signed manifests, provenance headers, and optional minimal watermarking for traceability. We will require build SBOM and CI/CD evidence (they can be redacted) for redistribution privileges.
- Commercials (initial proposal): annual named-customer redistribution license fee (USD, per named-customer tier), storage & snapshot costs (per-GB/month), and a per-instance standing support/SLO credit. We can share a modeled pricing sheet once you confirm target enterprise segments.
- Legal: partner addendum + indemnity language for IP misuse, export control clause, audit rights for redistributed instances, and explicit prohibition on downstream redistribution by customers. If OpenWeights requires the customer to hold raw weights, we will only accept that under escrow + explicit indemnity and pre-approved controls.

Attachments: Draft_Redistribution_Terms_v1.pdf (proposal + redlines).

Next steps we suggest:
1) Sign partner NDA/addendum (I can share our standard template or we can sign your addendum) — we attached a redline to speed discussion.
2) 30-minute sync with your engineering + legal (we are available Nov 20 or Nov 24 PST) to walk the controls and SBOM expectations.
3) 10-business-day technical due diligence window post-call (security artifacts + a lightweight load test on a non-prod model).

If that sounds workable, can you confirm availability for Nov 20 at 10:00am PT? Also please let us know if OpenWeights has a preferred redistribution fee structure (per-customer, per-instance, or revenue-share).

Looking forward —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
